newsitem.title: USA: First Brands says EPS estimates too high.
newsitem.headline: First Brands says EPS estimates too high.

text.p: Shares of First Brands Corp., maker of Glad plastic wrap and plastic bags, fell more than 12 percent Friday after the company warned that its earnings would fall short of Wall Street's projections.
First Brands traded as low as $22.75, down $3.25, in early activity on the New York Stock Exchange after the company issued its statement.
It said it expected the disappointing results, partly as a result of softness in the plastic wrap and plastic bag markets.

First Brands, which also makes the STP line of automotive products, said inventory reductions by automotive retailers and its above-average advertising and promotional spending also would dampen results.
The company said it expects its fourth quarter, ending June 30, to be profitable but that operating results may be 10 cents to 15 cents a share below year-earlier figures.
The company, based in Danbury, Conn., earned $18 million, or 43 cents a share, in the fourth quarter of 1996.
Wall Street analysts expected the company to earn 48 cents a share in the current quarter, according to estimates compiled by First Call prior to the company's warning.

First Brands said operating results for the first half of fiscal 1998 were likely to be slightly lower than the comparable 1997 period if market conditions did not improve immediately. But the company said profit should return to normal in the second half of fiscal 1998.

"Our closing of the financial statements for the month of May and the compilation of initial June customer orders, made it clear to us that we could not meet earnings estimates," said Chief executive officer William Stephenson.
First Brands also makes and markets pet products under the Scoop Away, Jonny Cat, Ever Clean and Ever Fresh names and Hearthlogg and Starterlogg products for home fire places.
